To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a sequence of moment generating functions converges to the moment generating function of a random vector if and only if the corresponding sequence of distribution functions converges weakly to a distribution function.

a sequence of moment generating functions converges to a moment generating function if and only if the corresponding sequence of distribution functions converges to the corresponding distribution function.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following two questions: (i) Under what conditions on a sequence of distribution function is it true that the sequence of the corresponding moment generating functions converges?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a sequence of probability distributions is weakly convergent if and only if the corresponding sequence of moment generating functions converges uniformly on a certain interval.
the convergence of a distribution function to a limit function $F(x)$ implies the convergence to the same limit function $F$ of the corresponding sequences of the moment generating functions.

the following three statements are mutually equivalent: (i) the sequence of distribution functions converges to a distribution function; (ii) the sequence of moment generating functions converges to an infinitely differentiable function; (iii) the sequence of the corresponding sequences of moments converges.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the results given in this paper are of a more general nature than those of [1] and [2] and that the proofs are more direct than those of the latter two papers.
the convergence of a distribution function to a limit distribution function is a sufficient condition for the corresponding convergence of the moment generating functions.

the results of the paper give a necessary and sufficient condition for the convergence of a bounded sequence of distribution functions in terms of the convergence of a corresponding sequence of their (finite) moment generating functions, which in turn is expressed in terms of the existence of a finite moment generating function for the limit distribution function.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the convergence of the moment generating function of a sequence of random variables does not necessarily imply the convergence of the sequence of random variables themselves.
, for the multivariate case, the convergence of a moment generating function sequence does not imply the convergence of the sequence of the corresponding distribution functions.
the convergence of a distribution function is equivalent to the convergence of the sequence of its moment generating functions.
